tracks.title: Ignition: The Forger's Call
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.suiteName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening
tracks.loreNote: The very first time in history that **"Ignition: The Forger's Call"** was ever played and recorded for a live concert release (previously, the only way to hear *Ignition* was to attend a CPI Home Football Game in person inside **The Crucible**). With no opening act—just CPI Alumni (*Class of 1989*) coming home to play for their alma mater—Ryan O'Connell rolls out to the edge of the stage in his manual chair, recalls the 1986 student contest cassette protected by 16-year-old Holly O'Connell's `$1.00` Perpetual Mutual Cross-License, and cues the stadium blackout. As Tyler strikes his steel brake drum and 65,000 Ironheads execute **The Stomp** on the galvanized bleachers of **The Anvil** until the Copernicus Hall seismographs spike, the four-piece rock band and the 300-piece **CPI Marching Forgers** erupt into a deafening call-and-response of **"IGNITION!"**

tracks.title: CPI Tech Triumph: The Marching Forgers
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.suiteName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening
tracks.loreNote: Directly out of the final anvil strike of *"Ignition"*, the Drum Major's whistle pierces the night air (`Tweet-Tweet-Tweet-Tweet!`) and **"The Engine Room"**—the high-tension Kevlar marching snare battery of the 300-piece **CPI Marching Forgers**—launches into the official Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute Fight Song. Forming the **CPI Hammer and Anvil** across the turf while 65,000 students and alumni clap in time and roar *"GO! FORGERS! FIGHT! FORGERS! WIN! CPI!"*, the Marching Forgers turn the opening minutes of the concert into the ultimate Saturday night inside The Crucible.

tracks.title: The Stardust Engine
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.suiteName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening
tracks.loreNote: While standard Stardust Engine concerts open directly with **"The Stardust Engine"**, here at their alma mater it serves as the culminating third movement of the opening sequence—performed with all 300 members of the **CPI Marching Forgers** still on the stage! Harmonizing 300 collegiate brass instruments and sousaphones with Cassidy's iconic 1986 **"Stardust"** analog synthesizer leitmotif and locking the Kevlar snare battery to Ryan's **"Engine"** guitar and Tyler's gated drums, the performance brings the stadium to a fever pitch before the Marching Forgers march off through the field tunnel—convincing everyone in the building that their guest appearance for the night is over.

tracks.title: Main Engine Start
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: As the main body of the Marching Forgers files into the tunnel (leaving their 20-piece Lead Brass & Drumline Honor Guard at the front lip of the turf), the core four-piece band—Cassidy on her wraparound synthesizers, Ryan in his manual chair at center-left on lead guitar, and identical twins Evan (bass) and Tyler (drums) on the back risers—backed on the stage-left riser by their 5-piece "Orbital Crew" stadium touring section (Marcus Vance on rhythm guitar, Darius "Doc" Holloway on second kit/percussion, Claire Lindqvist on auxiliary synths, and CPI Jazz soloists Prof. Julian Vance on trumpet and Elena Rostova on sax so not a single pre-recorded backing track is ever used on stage) slams straight into the 142 BPM countdown thriller from 2015's *Reignition*. Sixty-five thousand fans count down from ten to liftoff in unison.

tracks.title: Hard Reset
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: Rewinding to the 1997 title track that launched their independent stadium era after buying out their masters in 1996, Ryan and Cassidy trade blistering verses over Evan and Tyler's pounding arena rhythm section.

tracks.title: Not Your Doll
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: A massive stadium production number where Cassidy hands her wraparound synthesizer rig over to touring keyboardist Claire Lindqvist, throws on a black leather jacket, and takes the stage FRONT AND CENTER with a tilted chrome stand mic. As the 120-foot LED wall shatters a neon-pink porcelain doll mask into roaring crimson flames and twin columns of gold pyrotechnics erupt across the stage lip, Cassidy unleashes a ferocious, grit-soaked 1980s hard-rock belt tearing apart Apex Records' attempt to package her as their obedient 'Stardust' pop mascot.

tracks.title: Static
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: From 1995's independent cassette release *The Warehouse Tapes*. Ryan dedicates the song to the Class of '89 and the original CPI dormitory tape-traders who kept the band alive during the 1992–1995 Wilderness Years.

tracks.title: Midnight Drivers
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: As twilight deepens into blue hour over the Appalachian ridges behind the stadium press box, the band launches into the nocturnal title anthem of 2001's *Midnight Drivers*, honoring Evan and Tyler's decades behind the wheel on I-81.

tracks.title: Fifty-Two to Nothing: The Norfolk Reckoning
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: One of the loudest moments of the entire two-hour show. Pointing up at the North End Zone scoreboard of The Crucible—where sophomore **Jordan Shawn Kelly** (sitting in Accessible Field Section 104, Row A) had suffered his catastrophic `38–0` Homecoming meltdown against Virginia Dominion University (VDU) in September 2014—Ryan and Cassidy unleash the stadium stomper from 2015's *Reignition* celebrating CPI's retaliatory **52–0 shutout victory** in Norfolk, permanently overwriting the `38–0` ghost with 65,000 Forgers roaring *"FIFTY-TWO TO NOTHING! PUT IT ON THE BOARD!"*

tracks.title: The Contract
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: Because they are playing at home for their alma mater, the band digs deep into 2007's archival vault compilation *Lost Sounds*—performing **"The Contract"** live as a tribute to younger sister and CEO **Holly O'Connell** watching from the side of the stage.

tracks.title: Steel and Synthetics
tracks.discName: Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition
tracks.loreNote: A second live rarity pulled from 2007's *Lost Sounds* vault compilation, spotlighting the high-voltage interplay between Cassidy's analog synthesizer rig and Ryan's overdriven electric guitar right before the stadium floodlights cut to black for the cosmic centerpiece of the show.

tracks.title: Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.loreNote:
**THE LIVE ALBUM PREMIERE — THE ONLY RECORDED LIVE CONCERT PERFORMANCE OF *"ESCAPE VELOCITY (AD ASTRA)"* IN THE BAND'S ENTIRE CATALOG.** Originally written and recorded by **Cassidy O'Connell** in 1995 during the financial struggle of the band's Wilderness Years (*The Warehouse Tapes*) and later featured as the closing magnum opus of 1997's *Hard Reset* (Disc 2: *The Twin Moons*), this monumental four-movement progressive symphonic rock suite (*Part I: The Cage*, *Part II: Ignition [Ad Astra]*, *Part III: The Cosmos*, and *Part IV: Re-entry [The New World]*)—commonly known to Stardust Engine fans simply as *"Ad Astra"* when referring to it informally—is Cassidy's autobiography and what she considers her single most important piece of work. Because it had not been written yet during 1990's *Live in Chicago* and was omitted from the tighter two-hour waterfront amphitheater setlist of 2005's *Live in Norfolk*, **2016's *Live at the Crucible* is the ONLY live album where you can experience *"Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)"* performed live**.

To open **Act III: *Cosmic Tidal Lock*** in astrophysical launch order (achieving the `11.2 km/s` escape velocity required to break free of Earth's gravity before coasting to *Apoapsis* and locking into *Moon 1: Tidal Lock*), all four towering stadium floodlight banks inside The Crucible shut off completely, plunging 65,000 fans into the pitch-black Appalachian starfield while overhead planetarium lasers and the 120-foot curved LED screen transform the bowl into deep space. Across **13 minutes and 3 seconds** of uninterrupted live musicianship with **The Orbital Crew**, Cassidy journeys from the suffocating trauma of the 1992 *Friction* trial (*"The Shark was right, the nuke went off! / We won the battle, but at what cost?!"*), through the roaring rocket liftoff of *Ignition* (`0:00–6:30`) and the stadium-shaking **Main Engine Cutoff** applause at `6:30`, into the weightless zero-gravity sanctuary of *The Cosmos* (`6:30–10:45`, where she sings the line that defines the band's 1986 origin: *"This is the Stardust that is me! / The cosmos and the rocket's fire! / My one, my only true desire!"*), and finally into the triumphant stadium splashdown of *Part IV: Re-entry* (`10:45–13:03`), where all 65,000 Forgers roar ***"HELD BY THE SUN!"*** in unison before Cassidy whispers a breathless, deeply moved ***"Thank you so much..."*** into the microphone—bringing her 26-year journey from 1990's *"If You Walked Away"* full circle under the Blacksburg stars.

tracks.title: Apoapsis
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.loreNote: Having achieved escape velocity (`11.2 km/s`) to break free of Earth's gravity on the preceding 13-minute centerpiece, the vessel coasts upward to the highest point of its elliptical orbit on **"Apoapsis"**—the opening movement of **The Apoapsis Suite** from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset*. As the stadium bowl remains bathed in deep-space planetarium projections, Cassidy's shimmering analog synthesizers, Evan's floating fretless bassline, and Ryan's volume-pedal guitar swells recreate the weightless silence of deep space inside The Crucible.

tracks.title: Second Apoapsis
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.loreNote: The second movement of **The Apoapsis Suite** from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset*. Drawing structural inspiration from the sprawling, multi-part instrumental epics on **Origin**'s self-titled 1983 album, **"Second Apoapsis"** flows gaplessly out of *"Apoapsis"*, introducing cinematic tension and intricate interlocking synthesizer arpeggios between Cassidy O'Connell and touring keyboardist Claire Lindqvist before dissolving directly into the vocal finale of the suite, *"The Spectrum (True Color)"*.

tracks.title: The Spectrum (True Color)
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.loreNote: The sweeping vocal finale of **The Apoapsis Suite** from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset*. This progressive space-rock epic reimagines the band's 1987 debut single, *"Electric Color"*, from a sanitized corporate pop track into a sprawling observation of the cosmos (*"We left the atmosphere, the world was gray / The heavy gravity has finally faded away... And we are seeing the true spectrum! / A billion stars burning ultraviolet and blue"*). Performed here in **Act III: *Cosmic Tidal Lock***, it also serves as a brilliant mid-concert foreshadowing of the secret **Act VII True Ending**, when the band and all 300 **CPI Marching Forgers** will reclaim the original 1987 *"Electric Color"* as a blistering 1980s AOR Stadium Rock anthem to close the night.

tracks.title: Moon 1: Tidal Lock
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.loreNote: Culminating **Act III: *Cosmic Tidal Lock*** in astrophysical sequence (Escape Velocity $\rightarrow$ Apoapsis $\rightarrow$ Stable Orbital Capture), the stadium floodlights glow a deep cosmic indigo as Cassidy bathes all 65,000 fans in the signature anthem of **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** (from 1997's *Hard Reset* and 2003's *Sanctuary [Zero-G]*), turning the entire bowl of The Crucible into a weightless planetarium under the Blacksburg stars.

tracks.title: Moon 2: Roche Limit
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.suiteName: Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)
tracks.loreNote: Exploding directly out of the fading starfield of Cassidy's *"Moon 1: Tidal Lock"* to kick off **Act IV: *Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2 — Ryan's Heavy-Friction Orbit)***, **"Moon 2: Roche Limit"** (from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset* and Track 1 of Ryan's 2003 solo-led concept album *Mile Marker 98*) shatters the zero-gravity calm of the stadium with crimson strobe lights, pounding double-kit drums, and Ryan O'Connell's blistering, distorted electric guitar. Where Cassidy's *Moon 1* used the astrophysics of a tidal lock to celebrate stable, unbreakable loyalty, Ryan uses the **Roche limit**—the exact gravitational distance at which a satellite is torn to pieces by tidal forces—as a visceral, high-friction thesis statement confronting the trauma of the December 10, 1990 crash.

tracks.title: Impact (Mile Marker 98)
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.suiteName: Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)
tracks.loreNote: The visceral title cut of Ryan's 2003 concept album *Mile Marker 98* (*Moon 2*). Translating the night of December 10, 1990 into a cosmic collision in a treacherous debris field, **"Impact (Mile Marker 98)"** recounts how Ryan was cautiously piloting the band's 1988 Holt Freighter van at 40 MPH with hazard beacons active when a speeding vehicle clipped their rear quarter panel near Mile Marker 98, rolling the van twice and leaving Ryan pinned in the wreckage with a complete T10 spinal cord injury (*"We hit a massive fragment in the great unknown / At Mile Marker 98, I lost the throne! / We're barely alive, but we survived the night!"*).

tracks.title: Mayday: The Intercept
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.suiteName: Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)
tracks.loreNote: Directly answering the wreckage of *"Impact (Mile Marker 98)"*, Ryan and Cassidy unleash the high-friction arena-rock rescue anthem of 2003's *Mile Marker 98*—singing how Cassidy, Holly, Evan, and Tyler tracked his telemetry across the debris field after the 1990 Des Moines bus crash and pulled the Engine from the atmospheric fire.

tracks.title: Star City: Orbital Ward
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.suiteName: Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)
tracks.loreNote: Following the rescue of *"Mayday: The Intercept"*, **"Star City: Orbital Ward"** (from 2003's *Mile Marker 98*) slows the tempo into a brooding, heavy 1980s hard-rock power ballad that transposes Ryan's 1990 recovery at Star City General Hospital into an orbital medical bay. Translating the strict daily survival routines of **"Protocol T-10"**—the four-hour hydration and catheterization clock, the 15-minute wheelchair pressure weight shifts, and Evan and Tyler's synchronized "Freight Dog" twin-lifts—into the manual maintenance of a damaged but surviving starship, this performance directly sets the stage for the next Act (*Our Own Frequency*), where Ryan will strip away the sci-fi metaphors on *"Brother's Keeper"* and talk openly about how those daily ADLs led to tonight's decision to end global touring and stay home in Blacksburg.

tracks.title: Twin Moons: Touchdown
tracks.discName: Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite
tracks.suiteName: Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)
tracks.loreNote: Closing **Act IV: *Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)*** and uniting both halves of the 10-song *Twin Moons* cosmic journey (*Act III: Cosmic Tidal Lock* + *Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98*), **"Twin Moons: Touchdown"** is the triumphant sibling duet that concludes 2003's *Mile Marker 98*. Fusing Ryan's heavy, distorted 1980s arena-rock guitar with Cassidy's sweeping analog synthesizers in locked unison (*"The Engine and the Anchor locking into the groove / We finally found the gravity, we're ready to move! / Touchdown!"*), the song brings the vessel out of the freezing vacuum of space and sets it safely down on solid ground in Blacksburg—concluding with the Planetarium Narrator's sign-off (*"Atmospheric entry complete. Gravity is stable... Please exit safely, and welcome home"*) right as Evan and Tyler leave the stage for the intimate living-room acoustic block of **Act V: *Our Own Frequency***.

tracks.title: Our Own Frequency
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **Act V: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 1 of 4).** Recorded in complete secrecy in the living room of the Blacksburg house during the middle of the band's decade-long Burnout Hiatus, 2008's *Our Own Frequency* was never toured, promoted, or accompanied by press interviews—Ryan and Cassidy simply uploaded it to the Engine Room Records website on a Tuesday morning with a one-sentence note: *"We're still here, and we're okay."* Following the grand cosmic touchdown of *"Twin Moons: Touchdown"*, Evan and Tyler leave the stage completely, and the towering stadium light rigs dim to two solitary warm spotlights at center stage: Ryan in his wheelchair with an acoustic guitar, Cassidy at the piano, and two microphones. For the first time in front of a live audience, brother and sister strip away the stadium walls of sound to share their most private living-room conversation with their CPI family.

tracks.title: Brother's Keeper
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **Act V Centerpiece: *"Brother's Keeper"* — The Intimate Reality of Ryan's ADLs & The End of Touring / Forger Nation Summer Festival Announcement (Part 2 of 4).** The emotional centerpiece of 2008's *Our Own Frequency* and the most private, vulnerable song Ryan and Cassidy have ever written. *"Brother's Keeper"* is an unflinchingly intimate look at the life-or-death mutual protection between brother and sister and what Cassidy and the family go through every single day taking care of Ryan's **ADLs (Activities of Daily Living)** due to his T10 paralysis from the 1990 crash—performing his daily toileting requirements and morning anti-atrophy leg stretches, pushing his wheelchair when the road is steep, and sharing a bed pushed against the wall at night with Ryan on the inside and Cassidy sleeping on the outside edge to act as a **human bed-rail** so he doesn't roll off, while Ryan serves as Cassidy's emotional anchor against the overwhelming sensory and psychological toll of the world. Before playing the song in the pin-drop silence of The Crucible, Ryan explains that twenty-six years after the 1990 crash, the daily physical toll of those ADLs on the road has gotten too hard on his body and family—revealing that tonight's *Reignition* Tour finale at The Crucible is the **last concert a touring The Stardust Engine will ever play**. When the stadium gasps, Cassidy immediately reassures the crowd that they aren't retiring: to give the Town of Blacksburg and CPI time to plan, starting in **August 2017** (the first weekend of August), The Stardust Engine will stay home in Blacksburg to headline the annual **Forger Nation Summer Festival**—combining a campus-wide CPI Open House, a massive downtown Blacksburg block party for signed and unsigned bands, and The Stardust Engine's permanent annual residency concert + fireworks inside The Crucible.

tracks.title: Safe Person
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **Act V: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 3 of 4).** Drawn from 2008's *Our Own Frequency* living-room sessions, **"Safe Person"** answers the physical devotion of *"Brother's Keeper"* by revealing the other half of their unbreakable bond: how Ryan acts as Cassidy's safe person and emotional anchor when the flashing cameras, press questions, and autistic sensory overload threaten to overwhelm her. Performed strictly by Ryan on acoustic guitar and Cassidy at the piano with zero electric amps or stadium lights, sixty-five thousand Forgers hold up quiet white phone lights across the dark bowl of The Crucible.

tracks.title: Still Your Safe Person
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **Act V Finale: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 4 of 4 — Stripped-Down Piano & Acoustic Guitar Rendition).** Originally recorded as a full-band 1980s AOR studio power ballad on 2015's *Reignition*, Ryan and Cassidy strip **"Still Your Safe Person"** all the way down to strictly Cassidy's acoustic grand piano and Ryan's fingerpicked acoustic guitar—matching the living-room sanctuary of 2008's *Our Own Frequency*. Flowing directly out of *"Safe Person"* with zero drums, bass, or electric amps, brother and sister sing the seven-year sequel to their 2008 living-room vow (*"Still your safe person, after all these years / Still the quiet harbor when the world appears / Through the stadium thunder and the bright marquee / You can drop the armor when you look at me"*) as 65,000 fans hold up quiet white lights across the dark bowl of The Crucible.

tracks.title: Echoes in the Wire
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **Act VI Opener: Full-Band Electric Return (Permanently Replacing *"If You Walked Away"*).** Following the four-song *Our Own Frequency* brother-and-sister acoustic block, Evan and Tyler walk back onto the stage and strap on their electric bass and drum kit. Because 1989's *"If You Walked Away"* is permanently banned from all post-1990 Stardust Engine concerts to protect Cassidy from autistic sensory and abandonment overload, **"Echoes in the Wire"** (from 1997's *Hard Reset*) holds the emotional power-ballad spotlight—beginning at Cassidy's grand piano before Evan, Tyler, and Ryan's full electric stadium rig roars back to life.

tracks.title: Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **THE LIVE CONCERT DEBUT.** Although the studio recording of **"Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible"** (from 2004's *Progress Street*) first blasted over the stadium PA between the 3rd and 4th quarters on October 8, 2004, the band vowed they would **ONLY ever perform the song live when playing inside The Crucible** (deliberately omitting it even from 2005's *Live in Norfolk*). As the four massive Ironstone floodlight towers blaze at 100% power to kick off the fourth-quarter sprint of the concert, The Stardust Engine unleashes the live concert debut of *"Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible"* to a 65,000-voice roar of *"GO FORGERS! GO CPI!"*

tracks.title: Progress Street: Where the Fire Began
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: Singing about the house on Progress Street NE just a mile and a half north of the stadium, Ryan and Cassidy lead the entire lower bowl and student section in a jubilant 1980s AOR hometown singalong.

tracks.title: Neon on the Huckleberry Trail
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: Right after *"Progress Street: Where the Fire Began"*, Ryan and Cassidy celebrate the everyday Blacksburg sanctuary that kept the family whole during their ten-year hiatus: rolling along the **Huckleberry Trail**—the paved rail-trail connecting Blacksburg and Christiansburg—at twilight while the stadium floodlight towers of **The Crucible** glow like neon over the valley (*"Where nobody asks for a piece of our soul / And the mountain air makes the broken parts whole"*). Every fellow Forger in the 65,000-seat stadium roars the chorus back at the top of their lungs.

tracks.title: Neon Hearts
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: The band's 1989 hit title track, performed with the soaring 1980s arena-rock guitars and analog synth brass the band always wanted.

tracks.title: My Anchor Holds
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: One of the signature anthems from 1987's *Electric Color*, with 65,000 voices singing every word of the chorus back to the stage.

tracks.title: Reignition: Lights Up on Progress Street
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: The triumphant opening title anthem of 2015's *Reignition*, celebrating the family's return from their ten-year Burnout Hiatus and the permanent homecoming ahead in Blacksburg.

tracks.title: Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote: **THE FALSE ENDING.** To close what the audience believes is the end of the concert (and the final stop of their last world tour before beginning their annual CPI Summer Festival residency), the band performs the grand stadium power-ballad finale of 2004's *Progress Street*. As the drums and guitars slowly fade to a lone upright piano chord, Cassidy whispers *"Lights out on Progress Street..."*, Ryan says *"Goodnight, Forger Nation,"* and every stage light and Jumbotron screen inside The Crucible cuts to pitch black—convincing 65,000 fans that the concert is over.

tracks.title: Electric Color
tracks.discName: Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale
tracks.loreNote:
The secret 5-minute-26-second **Actual Ending** of the May 21, 2016 homecoming concert inside **The Crucible**—and the very first time in the band's 30-year history that **"Electric Color"** was ever performed as the blistering **1980s Album-Oriented Rock (Stadium Rock)** anthem Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler originally heard in their heads before Apex Records forced them to release it as a glossy 1987 Dance Synth-Pop single.

Right after the false ending of **"Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street"** plunged the stadium into darkness, all 300 members of the **CPI Marching Forgers** marched back out onto the stage in the pitch black (just as they had in the opening act of the show) to join the band. Protected prior to concert night by Holly O'Connell's **$300,000 collective student escrow ("The Forger Pot")** under Addendum No. 4 to her 1986 Cross-License—and disguised in the Marching Forgers' rehearsal folders as *"Exercise 87-B: The Anvil Finale"* with the vocal melody stripped out—for the first **1 minute and 40 seconds** (through Cassidy's spoken greeting over a lone piano chord, the Kevlar snare roll-off, and a massive 77-second AOR stadium guitar and 300-horn brass overture at `0:23–1:40`), not a single fan in the 65,000-seat stadium knew what song the band was playing, until **`1:40`** on the dot when the instruments dropped to a lone heavy kick drum and Cassidy sang the opening words of Verse 1: *"Woke up this morning, the world was gray..."*
